(Table 18.1). Among isomeric alcohols, the boiling points of straight chain alcohols are higher than that of branched.

The boiling points of alcohols are much higher than those of corresponding alkanes and alkyl halides. The high boiling points of is due to hydrogen bonding among the alcohol molecules.

Lower alcohols like methyl, ethyl and propyl alcohols are completely miscible with water. However the solubility of higher alcohols in water falls rapidly, due to increase in size of non-polar hydrophobic alkyl group.

18.1.3 Structure of Alcohols

Alcohols are alkyl derivatives of water molecules. Water molecule has an angular structure with H–O–H bond angle of 104.5°, which is slightly smaller than tetrahedral angle. Alcohol molecules have a similar geometry where C–O–H angle is higher than 104.5°, and the hybridization of oxygen is sp³. For example the C–O–H bond angle in methyl alcohol is 108.9° (Figure 18.1). The C–O and O–H bond lengths are 142 pm (1.42 Å) and 96 pm (0.96 Å) respectively.

Figure 18.1 Structure of water and methyl alcohol.

18.1.4 Acidity of Alcohols

The acidic nature of alcohol is due to presence of polar oxygen-hydrogen (O–H) bond in alcohols. R—O⁻ᵟ—H⁺ᵟ This allows the release of hydrogen atom as proton. Due to this acidic behaviour, alcohols react with sodium or potassium to form alkoxide salt with the liberation of hydrogen gas.

However, alcohols are very weakly acidic, and even less acidic than water, as clear from pKa values.

د الکول تېزابي طبیعت په الکولونو کې د قطبي اکسیجن–هایدروجن (O–H) تړون د شتون له امله دی. R—O⁻ᵟ—H⁺ᵟ دا د هایدروجني اټوم د پروټون په توګه ازادېدو ته اجازه ورکوي. د همدې تېزابي چلند له امله الکولونه له سوډیم یا پوټاشیم سره تعامل کوي او د هایدروجن ګاز له ازادېدو سره الکوکساید مالګه جوړوي.

خو الکولونه ډېر کمزوري تېزابي دي، حتی له اوبو هم لږ تېزابي دي، لکه څنګه چې د pKa له ارزښتونو څرګندېږي.

The boiling points of alcohols are much higher than those of corresponding alkanes and alkyl halides. The high boiling points of is due to hydrogen bonding among the alcohol molecules.

Lower alcohols like methyl, ethyl and propyl alcohols are completely miscible with water. However the solubility of higher alcohols in water falls rapidly, due to increase in size of non-polar hydrophobic alkyl group.

Table 18.1 Boiling and Melting Points of Some Alcohols

18.1.3 Structure of Alcohols

Alcohols are alkyl derivatives of water molecules. Water molecule has an angular structure with H–O–H bond angle of 104.5°, which is slightly smaller than tetrahedral angle. Alcohol molecules have a similar geometry where C–O–H angle is higher than 104.5°, and the hybridization of oxygen is sp³. For example the C–O–H bond angle in methyl alcohol is 108.9° (Figure 18.1). The C–O and O–H bond lengths are 142 pm (1.42 Å) and 96 pm (0.96 Å) respectively.

Figure 18.1 Structure of water and methyl alcohol.

18.1.4 Acidity of Alcohols

The acidic nature of alcohol is due to presence of polar oxygen-hydrogen (O–H) bond in alcohols. R—O⁻ᵟ—H⁺ᵟ This allows the release of hydrogen atom as proton. Due to this acidic behaviour, alcohols react with sodium or potassium to form alkoxide salt with the liberation of hydrogen gas.

However, alcohols are very weakly acidic, and even less acidic than water, as clear from pKa values.
